Fig. 2: Comparison between Conventional VR and BioMedVR. (a) Conventional VR methods (e.g., AttrVR) apply a single visual prompt to align input images with positive textual attributes (e.g., “well-defined, fluid-filled lesion”), but fail to handle visually similar yet semantically incorrect classes such as kidney cyst vs. kidney tumor, leading to overlapping latent embeddings. (b) In contrast, BioMedVR introduces a Confusionaware MoPE that employs visual experts—positive (δ+) and negative (δ−)—guided by descriptive and confusion-aware attributes respectively. The penalty region suppresses inter-class confusion in the embedding space. This design explicitly models fine-grained semantic conflicts, yielding more discriminative and well-separated representations in medical image diagnosis.
